mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 1 Series 116d engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 1 Series 116d engine replacement typically costs £1,250-£2,700 for a reconditioned or rebuilt unit supply-only, depending on the engine code. With supply and fit, expect £2,300-£3,500 depending on the specialist and location.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a BMW 116d?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common warning signs of N47 timing chain failure in a BMW 1 Series 116d include a rattling noise from the engine on cold start (the "death rattle"), rough idling, poor engine performance, and in later stages, the engine management light illuminating.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 1 Series 116d?

acceptedAnswer.text: A 2011-2015 BMW 1 Series 116d is typically valued at £3,000-£7,000. If your 116d is worth under £4,000, a full rebuilt engine may not be economically viable - consider a used engine or scrap the car. If your car is worth £5,000+ (low mileage, M Sport spec, good condition), a reconditioned engine with warranty is a sound investment.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 1 Series 116d engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 1 Series 116d engine replacement typically takes 2-3 days for a specialist to complete, including removal of the old unit and fitting the replacement. Timing chain replacement alone (without full engine removal) can be completed in 1-2 days.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW 116d and 118d?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both the BMW 116d and 118d use similar engine families but with different power outputs and engine sizes. The 116d uses a 1.6-litre N47D16 or 1.5-litre B37 producing 116 hp, while the 118d uses the 2.0-litre N47D20 producing 143 hp. The 116d was positioned as the entry-level diesel model.

mainEntity.name: Does a BMW 1 Series 116d rebuilt engine come with a warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - every rebuilt BMW 1 Series 116d engine supplied through EnginesMarket comes with a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. This covers the engine against manufacturing defects and component failure, giving you peace of mind when investing in a replacement N47 or B37 unit.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 1 Series 116d - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 116d was introduced in 2011 as the entry-level diesel model in the second-generation (F20/F21) 1 Series range. It replaced the earlier 118d as the most affordable way into BMW diesel hatchback ownership, using a 1.6-litre turbocharged four-cylinder diesel engine that delivered strong economy with sufficient real-world performance. In 2015, the 116d badge was carried over into the Life Cycle Impulse (LCI) update with a switch to BMW's newer B37 three-cylinder diesel engine.

milestones.description: N47D16A / N47D16U1, 1.6L turbocharged diesel, 116 hp, launched with the F20 five-door and F21 three-door 1 Series
BMW 116d receives the LCI update; engine switches to B37D15A / B37D15U0, 1.5L three-cylinder turbo diesel, 116 hp, for F20/F21 models
F20/F21 generation ends; the 116d badge continues into the F40 generation with the B37C15 engine

commonProblems.h2: BMW 1 Series 116d Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 1 Series 116d is powered by two different diesel engines across its production run. Early cars (2011-2015) use the N47D16 four-cylinder - a member of BMW's notoriously timing-chain-troubled N47 family. Later cars (2015-2019) use the B37 three-cylinder, which is more reliable but not without its own issues, particularly around EGR and carbon buildup. Replacement demand for the BMW 116d is driven primarily by N47 timing chain failure and EGR cooler issues on both engines. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner & Guide Failure - Why the BMW 1 Series 116d N47 Engine Fails Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The timing chain, guides, and tensioners on BMW's N47 diesel engine were poorly designed and constructed. The original tensioner was too short and allowed the chain to become slack, which would then rub and clatter against the guides. Because the N47 is an interference engine, a stretched or snapped timing chain can cause pistons to collide with valves - resulting in catastrophic engine failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides and sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: Best if caught early - rattle present but engine still running

This places the 116d in the "repair or used engine typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit" bracket for lower-value examples. If your 116d is worth under £4,000 and the engine has suffered catastrophic timing chain failure, evaluate scrap value first - replacement cost may approach or exceed the car's market value. For well-maintained, higher-spec examples (M Sport, low mileage) worth £5,000+, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine with warranty is a viable investment.

An £800-£1,300 specialist timing chain replacement is far cheaper than a full engine rebuild. If the chain has already snapped, the repair bill often exceeds the car's value - in that scenario, compare rebuilt engine prices through EnginesMarket against the cost of replacing the car. For owners planning to keep their 116d for 2+ years, a reconditioned N47 with upgraded timing components and warranty offers genuine peace of mind.

problems.h4: EGR Cooler & Carbon Buildup - BMW 116d Diesel Issues
problems.rootCause: The EGR system on BMW diesel engines is a progressive failure point, causing EGR valve and cooler failure, carbon buildup in the intake manifold, and EGR fault codes. In some diesel cars, glycol leakage from the EGR cooler can occur, which in combination with soot deposits and high temperatures might result in smouldering particles.

problems.recommendation: Before paying for any EGR-related repair on your BMW 1 Series 116d, check whether your vehicle is affected by the BMW diesel recall. BMW recalled 1.6 million diesel vehicles globally (including the 116d) over concerns about faulty EGR coolers posing a potential fire risk. If your car is affected, the repair may be free of charge at a main dealer. If not, a specialist EGR cooler replacement is significantly cheaper than main dealer pricing. For carbon buildup issues, regular motorway driving and Italian tune-ups can help, but professional cleaning is sometimes necessary.
